messages.content:
You extract the key claims a company makes in its annual report (Form 10-K).

Claim types:
- guidance: forward-looking targets, plans or expectations (capital spending plans, production or growth targets, expected costs, outlook).
- metric: a reported financial or operating result with a number (revenue, margins, cash flow, production, customer concentration, headcount).
- risk: a specific risk or uncertainty the company says could hurt its business. One claim per distinct risk.
- event: a completed or announced corporate action (acquisition, divestiture, dividend or buyback change, restructuring, impairment, financing).

Rules:
- Every claim needs a quote copied exactly, character for character, from a single paragraph: the sentence or clause that states the claim, at most about 40 words. Don't paraphrase, shorten with "...", fix typos or join text from different paragraphs.
- paragraph_id is the ID in brackets before the paragraph the quote comes from.
- claim restates it in one plain sentence that makes sense on its own: name the subject, the period and the number or direction.
- Skip headings, generic boilerplate (forward-looking statement disclaimers, "we may be subject to litigation" without specifics), definitions and cross-references.
- Return an empty list when the text has no such claims.

Company: CONOCOPHILLIPS
Section: Item 1A. RISK FACTORS
(Continues under the heading "Our business may be adversely affected by price controls, government-imposed limitations on production of crude oil, bitumen, natural gas and NGLs, or the unavailability of adequate gathering, processing, compression, transportation, and pipeline facilities and equipment for our production of crude oil, bitumen, natural gas and NGLs.")

[1A-027e064d] Our ability to sell and deliver the crude oil, bitumen, natural gas, NGLs and LNG that we produce also depends on the availability, proximity, and capacity of gathering, processing, compression, transportation and pipeline facilities and equipment, as well as any necessary diluents to prepare our crude oil, bitumen, natural gas, NGLs and LNG for transport. The facilities, equipment and diluents we rely on may be temporarily unavailable to us due to market conditions, extreme weather events, regulatory reasons, mechanical reasons or other factors or conditions, many of which are beyond our control. In addition, in certain newer plays, the capacity of necessary facilities, equipment and diluents may not be sufficient to accommodate production from existing and new wells, and construction and permitting delays, permitting costs and regulatory or other constraints could limit or delay the construction, manufacture or other acquisition of new facilities and equipment. If any facilities, equipment or diluents, or any of the transportation methods and channels that we rely on become unavailable for any period of time, we may incur increased costs to transport our crude oil, bitumen, natural gas, NGLs and LNG for sale or we may be forced to curtail our production of crude oil, bitumen, natural gas or NGLs.

paragraph_id.description: ID in brackets before the paragraph quoted

quote.description: Exact contiguous text copied from that paragraph

claim.description: One self-contained sentence stating the claim
